name: MemoryLeakSpec
source_title: Requested canonical CrySL raw source for MemoryLeak (not found: HTTP 404)
important_note: No published CrySL rule or documented API type named MemoryLeak was found. "unresolved.MemoryLeak" is a schema-preserving unresolved identifier, not a verified Java or Android API class. The representative messages evidence allocation failures only; they do not establish a retaining-reference memory leak, an API protocol violation, or responsibility of the reported methods.

events.name: outOfMemoryErrorTextObserved
events.condition: Observed when source, logs, or a finding contains one of these literal substrings. Its predicate is satisfied only when independently supported runtime evidence shows a java.lang.OutOfMemoryError attributable to the analyzed execution; a comment, catch block, fixture, or manually constructed message does not satisfy it.

events.name: outOfMemoryErrorRuntimeThrown
events.condition: Observed when a matching source construct is present. The predicate is not satisfied by source matching alone: a runtime allocation failure must be independently evidenced. An explicit throw or catch does not prove VM allocation failure or a memory leak.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That net.osmand.plus.render.MapRenderer.drawVectorTiles retains objects after they are no longer needed.
That com.simplemobiletools.gallery.pro.helpers.ThumbnailLoader.generateThumbnail retains objects after they are no longer needed.
That either representative finding is caused by a Java-heap leak rather than a single oversized or concurrent allocation.
That a direct/native byte-buffer allocation failure is equivalent to Java-heap exhaustion.
That an OutOfMemoryError establishes a CrySL protocol violation.
That a class named MemoryLeak belongs to java.lang, Android, OsmAnd, Simple Mobile Tools Gallery, or the CROSSINGTUD corpus.
That the two messages identify the same allocation domain, root cause, runtime configuration, or responsible library.
semantic_scope: At most, this provisional detector shape observes textual or runtime evidence of OutOfMemoryError-like allocation failure, including the supplied method-associated messages. No verified MemoryLeak CrySL API rule, target class, method signature, typestate order, constraint, or predicate was available. The reported application/library classes and methods are report locations, not evidence that either is the governed API type.

detector_semantics.claim: An analyzed execution or finding contains evidence of an out-of-memory allocation failure near a reported code location.
predicates: A finding or message contains an OutOfMemoryError-related literal.
Optionally, runtime evidence confirms that java.lang.OutOfMemoryError was thrown.
The report associates that evidence with a class and method location.
limitations: A text match is not proof that the error was thrown.
A thrown OutOfMemoryError is not proof of a memory leak.
The supplied findings provide neither heap-dump dominator evidence nor allocation/retention history.
No verified target API named MemoryLeak or CrySL event model was found.
The reported class and method names are application/library locations, not evidence that either is the governed API type.

documented_behavior: The documented Java platform API java.lang.OutOfMemoryError is thrown when the JVM cannot allocate an object because it is out of memory and garbage collection cannot make more memory available.
No authoritative documentation was found for an API type named MemoryLeak or for MemoryLeakSpec.
preconditions: For java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, an allocation attempt must fail because memory cannot be made available; the exact memory domain and detail message depend on JVM or runtime context.
A memory-leak conclusion requires additional retention evidence, such as a heap dump showing unexpected dominators or objects remaining reachable across expected lifecycle boundaries.

security_semantics.detector_claim: Possible out-of-memory failure evidence was observed at a reported location.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: The runtime failed to satisfy at least one allocation request; this may result from retained memory, workload size, allocation pressure, heap configuration, native-memory pressure, or other causes.

source_level: A primary source defining MemoryLeakSpec or MemoryLeak.crysl, including its SPEC target, EVENTS, ORDER, CONSTRAINTS, REQUIRES, and ENSURES sections.
A verified fully qualified API type whose simple name is exactly MemoryLeak.
If the rule is local, the repository path, revision, and rule-loader mapping from MemoryLeakSpec to its source file.
runtime: A stack trace or crash record proving a runtime java.lang.OutOfMemoryError and preserving its exact detail message.
Heap-dump and dominator/reference-path analysis to establish unexpected object retention for a Java-heap leak claim.
Native/direct-memory diagnostics for buffer or renderer allocation failures, plus allocation size, memory limits, and concurrent-workload data.
Reproduction under controlled heap and device/runtime settings.
compatibility: Device ABI, graphics backend, and renderer/library versions for vector-tile allocation failures.
Media codec and thumbnail-extraction implementation versions for 4K-video thumbnail allocation failures.
Configured heap, direct-memory, process-memory, and graphics-memory limits.

known_false_positive_shapes: A one-time or short-lived allocation exceeds the configured Java heap while no objects are improperly retained.
Parallel vector-tile rendering creates transient peak memory pressure without a persistent leak.
Generating a 4K video thumbnail requires a transient decoded frame or bitmap larger than available memory.
The failure originates in direct/native, graphics, codec, or JNI allocation rather than the Java heap.
The matching text occurs in a log fixture, test, comment, catch block, or synthetic exception message.
The method is merely the allocation site; the actual retained-object owner is elsewhere.
The heap limit is insufficient for the intended workload or device class.
